name: Aardwolf ASCII Map
author: Solao
description: The MUD's ASCII map, scaled to fit its panel with colours intact. Capture mechanism from MudForge's ASCII Map Widget example.
script:
--[[ aw-ascii-map.lua Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-05 Aardwolf's ASCII map, drawn to fit the panel, with its colours intact. CREDIT: this began as the "ASCII Map Widget" example that ships with MudForge, written by MudForge (Asmodeus). What is theirs is the capture MECHANISM, and it is a good one — a wildcard trigger that exists from the start and is only ENABLED between the markers, so nothing runs Lua against every line of a session. That is kept because it is right. What is NOT theirs: the markers. Their example reads {map_start} and {map_end}; Aardwolf sends and , and Sean had already made that change before this rewrite started. Three things are different again. IT SCALES. The original drew at a fixed 16px, so the only way to make a map denser was to shrink the window around it, and a window smaller than the map clipped it. This measures the map, measures the panel, and picks the largest size that fits — up as well as down. IT IS HTML, NOT CANVAS. Everything else in this set is an html widget with one stylesheet, so a canvas map was the one panel that looked like it came from somewhere else. Colour survives the sanitiser the same way the shop panel does it: inline colour is stripped, so each distinct colour becomes a generated class in the single \n", seen end local function render() if not widget then return end local css, cls = css_for() local cols, rows = extent() local bar = 'ASCII Map' .. '' .. '
hide
' local body if #lines == 0 then body = '
No map yet — turn it on in game with ' .. 'map on.
' else local size = fit(cols, rows) local out = {} for _, line in ipairs(lines) do local ok, segs = pcall(parseAnsiText, line) if not ok or type(segs) ~= "table" then table.insert(out, esc(line)) else local row = "" for _, seg in pairs(segs) do if type(seg) == "table" and type(seg.text) == "string" then local hex = (type(seg.color) == "string") and string.match(seg.color, "^#%x%x%x%x%x%x$") or nil local k = hex and cls[hex] or nil if k then row = row .. '' .. esc(seg.text) .. "" else row = row .. esc(seg.text) end end end table.insert(out, row) end end -- font-size in an inline style is geometry, which the sanitiser keeps body = '
'
            .. table.concat(out, "\n") .. "
" end setWidgetProperty(widget, "content", css .. '
' .. bar .. '
' .. '
' .. body .. '
') end --- -- capture -- -- The wildcard trigger is created once, disabled, and only enabled between the -- markers. That is MudForge's design and it is the right one: a permanently -- armed catch-all runs Lua against every line the MUD sends. -- -- Enabling it from inside the callback works for the one reason it -- usually wouldn't — the trigger already exists, so this flips a flag rather -- than creating a trigger mid-packet. One CREATED there would never see the -- rest of that packet, which cost this codebase an evening elsewhere. --- local function on_start() buf = {} if rowTrig then pcall(enableTrigger, rowTrig) end return false end local function on_row(c, line, w, raw) table.insert(buf, (type(raw) == "string" and raw ~= "") and raw or tostring(line or "")) return false end local function on_end() if rowTrig then pcall(disableTrigger, rowTrig) end lines = tighten(buf) buf = {} render() return false end function init() widget = createWidget({ type = "html", name = "map", title = "ASCII Map", position = { x = 60, y = 60 }, size = { width = 460, height = 420 }, appearance = { showTitleBar = false, autoHideSettingsCog = true, }, }) -- registered disabled; the markers switch it on and off rowTrig = addTrigger("*", on_row, { type = "wildcard", priority = 1, keepEvaluating = false, omitFromOutput = true, enabled = false, }) addTrigger("^\\s*$", on_start, { type = "regex", priority = 80, keepEvaluating = false, omitFromOutput = true }) addTrigger("^\\s*$", on_end, { type = "regex", priority = 80, keepEvaluating = false, omitFromOutput = true }) -- a resized panel is a different font size, and nothing else changes --[[ Clear first. init() runs again on every hot-reload and registerWidgetEvent APPENDS — so each reload stacks another handler on the same widget and one click fires all of them. It shows up as buttons sending their command two, three, five times, getting worse the longer a session goes on, and nothing about it looks like a plugin bug from the outside. unregisterWidgetEvent with no callback drops every handler for the event, which is exactly what a fresh init wants. ]] drop_handlers(widget, "resize") registerWidgetEvent(widget, "resize", function() render() end) drop_handlers(widget, "action") registerWidgetEvent(widget, "action", function(data) if type(data) ~= "table" then return end if tostring(data.action or "") == "close" then hideWidget(widget) end end) local saved = loadTable("aw_ascii_map") if type(saved) == "table" then local z = tonumber(saved.zoom) if z and z >= FS_MIN and z <= FS_MAX then zoom = z end if saved.labels == true then labels = true end end render() registerCommand("awmap", function(args) local a = args if type(a) == "table" then a = table.concat(a, " ") end a = string.lower((string.gsub(tostring(a or ""), "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1"))) if a == "hide" then hideWidget(widget) elseif a == "labels" then labels = not labels saveTable("aw_ascii_map", { zoom = zoom, labels = labels }) lines = tighten(lines) -- re-trim what we already have render() utilprint(TAG .. (labels and "keeping the room name and exits." or "map only - the room name and exits are already on screen.")) elseif string.match(a, "^zoom") then local n = tonumber(string.match(a, "^zoom%s+(%d+)$")) if string.match(a, "^zoom%s+fit$") or a == "zoom 0" then zoom = 0 saveTable("aw_ascii_map", { zoom = 0, labels = labels }) render() utilprint(TAG .. "back to fitting the panel.") elseif n then if n < FS_MIN then n = FS_MIN end if n > FS_MAX then n = FS_MAX end zoom = n saveTable("aw_ascii_map", { zoom = zoom, labels = labels }) render() utilprint(TAG .. "pinned at " .. zoom .. "px.") else utilprint(TAG .. (zoom > 0 and ("pinned at " .. zoom .. "px.") or "fitting the panel.") .. " '/awmap zoom " .. FS_MIN .. "-" .. FS_MAX .. "' to pin, '/awmap zoom fit' to stop.") end elseif a == "clear" then lines = {} render() utilprint(TAG .. "cleared.") elseif a == "" or a == "show" then showWidget(widget) render() else local cols, rows = extent() utilprint(TAG .. "the MUD's ASCII map, scaled to fit its panel.") utilprint("$w /awmap show it") utilprint("$w /awmap hide put it away") utilprint("$w /awmap labels keep the room name and exits, or not") utilprint("$w /awmap zoom pin a size, or fit the panel") utilprint("$w /awmap clear forget the last map") utilprint(TAG .. ((rows > 0) and (rows .. " row(s), " .. cols .. " column(s), drawn at " .. fit(cols, rows) .. "px" .. ((zoom > 0) and " (pinned)" or " (fitted)") .. ", panel " .. select(1, panel_size()) .. "x" .. select(2, panel_size()) .. ".") or "nothing captured yet - 'map on' in game.")) end end, "the MUD's ASCII map, scaled to fit its panel") end --[[ A reload would otherwise strand the old wildcard trigger, and a catch-all with omitFromOutput left behind swallows the session. ]] function cleanup() if rowTrig then pcall(removeTrigger, rowTrig); rowTrig = nil end end
